analytic_results.claim: For either sigma in {ell,u}, let p*_sigma be the Gaussian block likelihood maximized only over mu in [-h,h]. For every block mean ybar and centered SSE W, fbar_sigma <= c_sigma p*_sigma with c_sigma=exp[-m h^2/(2 sigma^2)]. W cancels. By symmetry take ybar>=0. If 0<=ybar<=h, fbar_sigma/p*_sigma=exp[-m(ybar^2+h^2)/(2 sigma^2)] cosh(m h ybar/sigma^2), whose log derivative is (m/sigma^2)[-ybar+h tanh(m h ybar/sigma^2)] <= (m/sigma^2)(kappa_sigma-1)ybar <0 because kappa_sigma=m h^2/sigma^2<1. If ybar>=h, the ratio is [1+exp(-2m h ybar/sigma^2)]/2, decreasing in ybar; at ybar=h it is <=exp(-kappa_sigma/2) because kappa_sigma<=kappa_ell=0.41031041441890028 < (2/3)log 2 =0.46209812037329687. Thus the global maximum is ybar=0 and equals c_sigma.

Since p*_sigma<=p_max over the full Gaussian null rectangle, p_rho0 <= Cmix*p_max for Cmix=rho0*c_ell+(1-rho0)*c_u. High-precision evaluation gives c_ell=0.81452088708637345, c_u=0.85624197674620692, Cmix=0.83311107702299158 and M*Cmix=0.85253939777098174. Therefore for every possible 32-sample block, E_scaled/E_UI=p_max/(M*p_rho0)>=1/(M*Cmix)=1.1729663199314464, equivalently log E_scaled-log E_UI>=0.15953585649820393 nat. This is a pathwise bound, not a distributional or Monte Carlo statement.

The retained delayed-start recursion A_k=e_k(A_{k-1}+pi_k), M_k=A_k+T_k is coordinatewise monotone in every current multiplier e_k and in prior A. With identical initialization, start weights, variance channels and portfolio weights, r103b implies the scaled universal-channel state is at least the r85 UI state at every update by induction. The full 0.25 variance-up / 0.25 variance-down / 0.50 universal portfolio is therefore pathwise no smaller at every monitoring time. Under any common threshold and any common data trajectory, replacing UI by the safe scaled four-corner factor cannot delay the alarm.
